title: Tech Note: Converting Arrays to HTML Tables
author: David Adams and Forrest Swilling
featured_technology: Netscape Navigator HTML table tags (HTML 3.0 draft)

historical_commentary.text: This note documents a hand-rolled 4D procedure (ArraysToTable) for generating HTML <TABLE> markup from 4D arrays, targeting the then-new Netscape-extended HTML 3.0 table tags; the specific need to manually assemble HTML strings from arrays is obsolete in an era of modern templating, ORDA-based REST/JSON APIs, and client-side rendering frameworks, but the underlying pattern of procedurally generating markup from structured data remains conceptually familiar.
related_updates: 4D's web capabilities have since gained a built-in web server, WebArea/QuickReport-style tools, and ORDA/REST endpoints, making manual per-tag HTML string concatenation unnecessary for most modern use cases
The Netscape-specific HTML table tags described here were later formalized and superseded by standard HTML4/HTML5 and CSS-based table styling
Global procedures are called Project Methods since 4D v6 (1997), and file/table naming and array-parameter idioms shown here reflect the pre-V6 language
